rationale: Interpreted the healing-phase successor receipt and recorded the durable fact it establishes. Receipt 455e647ad0794a16903414b5a8846276 parsed four events and evaluated all ten comparisons: the carried-over seven behave exactly as in the previous run (five violated witnesses at indices 1 and 2, two controls holding), and the two new healed-phase assertions are violated at event index 3 - the nodes still hold different payloads at the conflict index with the same term (A and C minority-write against B, D and E majority-write, all term 3), and the restarted node still reports {A,B,C} after the cluster is whole again and committing, with its log advancing to index 12 as the progress control confirms. The child question's third limitation (post-healing fate of the conflicting entry) is therefore resolved, the parent's persistence limitation narrows to long-run persistence, and the AppendEntries reconciliation behaviour behind the permanent divergence is recorded as reusable knowledge. Also filed an experiment for the other registered question in this feature: a harness that builds a snapshot at index 1000 plus 9000 committed LogCommand entries above it and constructs the node in both modes. Local construction feedback showed the first fixture attempt with LogNoop entries returned immediately because prepareLog never sends no-ops to the FSM, so the entries were changed to the commit path; the feature-on case then failed to return within the 5s window while the identical fixture with the feature off returned with lastApplied still at the snapshot index, which isolates the replay as the cause.

knowledge.statement: Two entries that end up at the same log index with the same term but different payloads on different servers are never reconciled by AppendEntries: the receiver truncates its suffix only when an incoming entry at an existing index has a different term, and an entry whose index and term match the stored one is skipped as a duplicate before any configuration or log processing, so the divergence persists while the cluster continues to commit later entries.
knowledge.conditions: AppendEntries conflict handling (raft.go 1526-1553) on a follower whose stored entry at that index has the same term; observed after the split-leader window of the RestoreCommittedLogs restart defect was healed with a further committed entry and no snapshot install.

interpretations.rationale: This revision reproduces the split-brain window and adds the healing phase; every assertion is contradicted or confirmed as predicted. Admission index 0 again establishes snapshot index 6 with {A,B,C}, the committed configuration entry at index 8 with {A,B,C,D,E} and a stored commit index of 8 covering it. After the restart (index 1) the node reports {A,B,C}. In the split (index 2) A leads the two-voter partition while D leads the other three, so leader_count is 2, both leaders commit at index 11 in term 3 with different payloads, and the minority leader's write commits, while the in-partition control C never leads and the majority keeps reporting {A,B,C,D,E} (comparisons 5 and 6 hold). New in this revision, after the partition is healed, one further entry is committed and the cluster is whole (index 3): the payloads at index 11 remain different on different nodes with the same term 3 (A,C minority-write against B,D,E majority-write), so the entries cannot be reconciled by term comparison (comparison 7 violated), and the restarted node's own view is still {A,B,C} although its log advanced to index 12 and the current leader reports {A,B,C,D,E} (comparison 8 violated, comparison 9 holds as the progress control). Comparison-level basis for the persistence is knowledge @same_term_divergence_unrepairable for the entry divergence and the duplicate-skip behaviour for the configuration: the leader never re-sends the committed configuration entry to a log that already stores it, and a same-term duplicate is skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry. Limits: the healed sample is one window after a single further entry, in-memory stores, a graceful shutdown instead of a crash and a transport-only partition; the healed leader varied across runs (in this receipt D; local repeats produced A once and D or E otherwise), so the receipt does not claim that the stale node leads a healed cluster; and whether a snapshot install or log compaction eventually repairs the divergent entries is unobserved.
limitations: The healed observation is a single sample after one further committed entry; no long run, no further membership change and no snapshot install is covered.
The healed leader identity varies between runs, so nothing is concluded about which node leads after healing.
In-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown of the restarted node rather than a crash.
counterevidence: In this receipt the healed cluster elected D, a node with the current configuration, so the stale node does not always lead once the partition is removed.
The progress control holds: the restarted node's log advanced after healing, so the stale view is not a symptom of a stalled or isolated node.

interpretations.rationale: Answer, now with the post-split phase observed: yes. A node left with a stale configuration by the RestoreCommittedLogs replay wins an election with fewer votes than the configuration recorded in its own committed log while the remaining voters elect their own leader, and the damage outlives the partition. Receipt b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e gives the split window (A leading two voters, D or B leading three, both committing at index 11 in term 3), and receipt 455e647ad0794a16903414b5a8846276 repeats that window and then heals it, showing that after a further committed entry the five nodes still disagree about the payload at index 11 while agreeing on its term, and that the restarted node still uses {A,B,C} although its log advanced to index 12 and the serving leader knows {A,B,C,D,E}. The mechanism chain is the parent question's scan defect plus three source rules: quorum and voter set from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096), votes admitted from the voter's own view (raft.go 1660-1680), and AppendEntries truncating only on term difference while skipping same-term duplicates (raft.go 1526-1553). Scope: one cluster and one partition window per run, in-memory stores, a graceful restart, a healed sample rather than a long run, and the no-feature restart control still unexecuted (the in-partition sibling C and the feature-off construction experiment carry the contrast).
limitations: One cluster per run with a single partition window and a single healed sample.
In-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown rather than a crash.
The no-feature restart control inside the cluster remains unexecuted.
No snapshot install, log compaction or long run after healing is observed.
counterevidence: The in-partition control C, with the current configuration, never leads in either receipt, so the partition alone does not explain the election.
After healing the cluster elected a node with the current configuration in this receipt, so the persistence claim is about the restarted node's own view rather than about it retaining leadership.
The restarted node's log advances normally, so nothing about its participation or connectivity explains the stale view.

interpretations.joint_history: Three receipts of two fixed experiment families over one defect chain. The first constructs the restart state in harness-supplied stores and reads the resulting configuration, quorum and FSM queue. The second produces the same state through normal operations (bootstrap, election, membership change, user snapshot, restart) and observes the split; the third is a revision of that harness which adds the healing phase, and its diff is limited to the reconnect, the extra apply and the healed sampling, so its carried comparisons and events are the same scenario and are not additive evidence for the carried predicates. Compatibility rests on identical structural conditions in every receipt: snapshot configuration {A,B,C}, a committed configuration entry with {A,B,C,D,E} above the snapshot, and a persisted commit index covering it (first receipt event index 2, second event index 0, third event index 0), with the restarted node reporting {A,B,C} in each (indices 3, 1 and 1 respectively). No value is combined across receipts; every comparison outcome is read from its own receipt.
interpretations.rationale: Current account: with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a CommitTrackingLogStore whose persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft never rebuilds the node's configuration from that entry, so the restarted node keeps the snapshot's membership for candidate admission and election quorum; that stale view lets it lead with two votes where the current configuration requires three, produces two concurrent leaders with conflicting commits at the same index and term, and the stale view survives the partition being healed while the node keeps participating. Basis: restoreFromCommittedLogs reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) (api.go 724-753); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 (api.go 610-620) above the committed configuration entry, which is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry; quorum and voter admission come from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096, 1660-1680); duplicates are skipped so no later AppendEntries reprocesses the entry (raft.go 1526-1553); and the persisted commit index exists only because the node ran with the feature enabled (raft.go 1393-1403). Witnesses: receipt f4adc58c4125434eb91cacf438a6da50 for the configuration and quorum state on supplied stores (feature on: {A,B,C}, quorum 2; feature off: {A,B,C,D,E}, quorum 3), receipt b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e for the split (A leads two voters, three others elect their own leader, conflicting commits at index 11 term 3, minority commit accepted), and receipt 455e647ad0794a16903414b5a8846276 for the healed state (divergent payloads at index 11 with equal terms remain, the restarted node stays at {A,B,C} while its log advances to 12). Remaining limits: persistence is now observed across the healed window but not over a long run, further membership changes or a snapshot install; the restart is graceful with in-memory stores and scaled timeouts; no no-feature restart control was run inside the cluster; and the divergence is only shown to persist for the sampled window. The first filed experiment's receipt 99718ab469974eb1ad40516efe7c999e stays a retained channel failure with no evaluated comparison.
limitations: Persistence is observed across one healed window; no long run, further configuration change or snapshot install is covered.
Both cluster receipts use in-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown instead of a crash.
The partition is transport-only and the healed state is sampled once after a single further committed entry.
No no-feature restart control was executed inside the cluster; the contrast comes from the in-partition sibling and the feature-off construction experiment.
counterevidence: The node stores the newer committed configuration entry and replays it to the FSM, so repair through a later configuration entry, an installed snapshot or log compaction is not excluded; only the observed paths fail to refresh it.
A deployment that never ran with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled stores commit index 0, in which case the scan covers the entry and no divergence occurs.

The in-partition control C never leads in either cluster receipt, and after healing the cluster elected a node holding the current configuration, so the defect explains a minority leader and a persistent stale view rather than permanent stale leadership.

scope.description: A single node (LocalID A) constructed in two modes from the same in-memory stores: a version-1 snapshot at index 1000 with configuration {A} and a log of 9000 committed LogCommand entries above it (indices 1001..10000), with the commit-tracking store reporting commit index 10000; RestoreCommittedLogs off versus on, with normal initialization in both cases.
assumptions: The fixture is supplied by the harness (snapshot, 9000 entries, staged commit index); it is the restart-shaped state a node running with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled can reach, with the commit index persisted atomically with the log entries by the store contract.

The number of batches the replay produces is derived from MaxAppendEntries (64) and the entries above the snapshot (9000), giving 141 batches, and is emitted as an operand rather than asserted from a constant.
Non-return is evaluated by constructing in a goroutine and waiting 5s; the control uses the identical fixture with the feature off, so a slow fixture, slow store or slow FSM is excluded as the cause.
The feature-on node that never returns cannot be shut down; its goroutine is abandoned when the test process exits.
excluded: No on-disk store is exercised; the in-memory CommitTrackingLogStore is used.
The blocked constructor is not resumed, so no recovery path after the stall is observed.

experiment.prefix: The harness builds fresh InmemTransport("A"), InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots) per mode; writes a version-1 snapshot at index 1000, term 1 with configuration {A} at configuration index 1 and closes the sink; stores 9000 LogCommand entries at indices 1001..10000 in batches of 256; and calls logs.StageCommitIndex(10000). It emits a 'fixture' event with the fixture operands (snapshot index, log last index, stored commit index, entries above the snapshot, MaxAppendEntries, batches required, observation window), then builds Config from DefaultConfig() with LocalID "A", a null logger and RestoreCommittedLogs set from the mode, and calls NewRaft(conf, probeFSM, logs, stable, snaps, trans) in a goroutine. A 'construct' event reports newraft_returned and, when the constructor returned, its last applied index, queued FSM batches and the observed FSM mutation channel capacity. Modes run in order replay_off, replay_on; the probe FSM discards applied entries and accepts the snapshot bytes.
experiment.responsibility: hashicorp/raft NewRaft startup path: restoreFromCommittedLogs replays committed entries through processLogs into fsmMutateCh before the constructor starts runFSM.

knowledge.assertion: restoreFromCommittedLogs calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) before the configuration scan and before background goroutines start

comparisons.description: With the replay enabled, construction should return within the observation window.
Control: the identical fixture with the feature off should construct normally.
Control operand: without the replay the FSM is not advanced past the snapshot, so the comparison is about the replay and not about the fixture's size.
